item.title: Tinubu Proposes ₦1.01 Trillion for INEC in 2026 Budget Ahead of 2027 Polls
item.description: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has allocated a historic ₦1,013,778,401,602 (approximately ₦1.01 trillion) to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in the 2026 Appropriation Bill presented to the National Assembly.This substantial funding one of the largest single allocations ever made to the electoral body comes as preparations intensify for the 2027 general elections.The figure is contained in the detailed breakdown of the 2026 budget released by the Budget Office of the Federation.

item.title: Family Escapes Death as Tomato-Laden Truck Crashes into Vehicles on Otedola Bridge
item.description: A serious road accident occurred around noon today on the Otedola Bridge section of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway when a mini truck carrying a large load of tomatoes suddenly lost control, reportedly due to brake failure.The truck veered across lanes and collided with several vehicles, including cars and SUVs, causing extensive damage and scattering tomatoes across the roadway. item.description: Justice Emmanuel Subilim of the National Industrial Court in Abuja has granted an interim order restraining the National Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) and its members from proceeding with the indefinite strike scheduled to begin at midnight on January 12, 2026.The ex-parte order was issued on Friday following an urgent application filed by the Federal Government of Nigeria and the Attorney General of the Federation. item.title: FG Proposes N100bn in 2026 Budget to Clear Debts Owed to Local Contractors
item.description: The Federal Government has set aside N100 billion in the proposed 2026 Appropriation Bill to pay off outstanding debts owed to indigenous (local) contractors nationwide, as part of measures to address persistent payment delays in the public sector.The allocation, listed under “Payment of Local Contractors’ Debts/Other Liabilities” in the service-wide vote, is aimed at providing much-needed relief to Nigerian-owned companies for work already executed on government projects.
